problems.title: Conditional asymmetry does not identify a physical cause
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, Eq.(1), PDF p.4; Limitations, PDF p.9
claim: The asymmetry \(P(A\mid B)\ll P(B\mid A)\) motivates a directional dependency heuristic.
analysis: For positive joint probability, \(P(A\mid B)/P(B\mid A)=P(A)/P(B)\). Independent events with marginals \(0.01\) and \(0.9\) have joint \(0.009\), giving the large conditional asymmetry despite independence. The same identity holds under a common fixed context. The curated benchmark additionally selects physical-support pairs, and the paper explicitly describes its approach as statistical co-occurrence without causal reasoning.
result: The comparison alone is not causal identification. This scoped limitation does not contradict the qualified heuristic or its reported benchmark arithmetic.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper correction is required for this cleared concern.
problems.impact_rationale: A heuristic-scope clarification, without a demonstrated substantive error.

problems.title: Mean similarity does not uniquely specify distributional peakedness
claim: The product of mean CLIP/DINO similarities is motivated by peakedness of the inpainting distribution.
analysis: In both feature spaces take original unit vector \((1,0)\) and candidate outputs \((0.6,0.8)\), \((0.6,-0.8)\), with area fraction \(1\). Both rescaled similarities are \(0.8\). A point mass and an equal two-point mixture have entropy \(0\) and \(\log2\), but score \(1-0.8^2=0.36\) in both cases. Real-image realizability of these simultaneous embeddings is unestablished.
result: The score measures deviation from the original crop and need not identify entropy. Its empirical utility is not contradicted.
